Rarity.rationale: TouchOfOrobas.cs:27. Granted by the ported Orobas shrine (events/orobas.py:72). Executed: `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py pool` -- Ancient rarity is not in the grab bag, the shrine is the only path.

AfterObtained.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and N4 per binding rule 4. The core behaviour is right and executed: the starter relic is replaced IN PLACE by its refinement and the replacement's own after_obtained runs. What the port drops from RelicCmd.Replace -> Obtain is the grab-bag strip (G1, dormant) and, for a starter outside the refinement map, the Circlet fallback (N4, waiver -- other characters).

guards.what: N1 (EXECUTED): RelicCmd.Replace's index preservation and the AfterObtained call on the replacement
guards.rationale: RelicCmd.Replace (RelicCmd.cs:74-82) records `player.Relics.IndexOf(original)`, calls Remove(original), then `Obtain(replace, player, indexOfOriginal)` -- so the refinement occupies the starter's slot, which matters because the relic list order is the hook-listener order (CombatState.cs:428-435) and Burning Blood is index 0 (audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json's meat_on_the_bone finding turns on exactly that). touch_of_orobas.py:31 does `run.relics[run.relics.index(starter)] = upgraded`, preserving the index, and :32 calls `upgraded.after_obtained(run)`, which is Obtain's `await relic.AfterObtained()` (RelicCmd.cs:53). EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py orobas-replace`): relics go from ['burning_blood'] to ['black_blood', 'touch_of_orobas'] -- Black Blood at index 0, exactly where Burning Blood was. Rule 7: RelicCmd.cs, run.py and audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): RelicCmd.Obtain strips the obtained relic from both grab bags (`player.RelicGrabBag.Remove(relic)` and `runState.SharedRelicGrabBag.Remove(relic)`, RelicCmd.cs:41-45) and stamps `FloorAddedToDeck`; the port's direct list assignment does neither
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the port bypasses RunState.add_relic (run.py:546-553) entirely -- it writes into run.relics itself -- so nothing removes the replacement from the run's grab bag and a later pull could offer the same relic a second time. (RunState.add_relic does not strip the bag either, which is a separate shared question this record does not own.) REACHABILITY (DORMANT, executed -- same probe): the only refinement the Ironclad sim can reach is black_blood, and `black_blood` is NOT in the run's relic grab bag beforehand (the probe reports 'no'), so there is nothing to strip and no duplicate pull is possible. The refinement relics are not grab-bag relics in the transcribed pools (relic_pools.py). What would make it live: adding any refinement relic to a grab bag, or porting a second character's refinement pair. FloorAddedToDeck has no sim counterpart at all and no ported reader (`grep -rn floor_added sts2_rl/` finds nothing), which is the same shape and is folded in here rather than given its own entry. Rule 7: run.py and relic_pools.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N2: `RelicCmd.Remove(original)` awaits `original.AfterRemoved()` (RelicCmd.cs:61-66); the sim's Relic base declares no after_removed and the port calls nothing
guards.rationale: VOCABULARY RULING (2026-07-26 relic fix pass), applied at every dead-in-the-source site in this tier so it stops contradicting itself. When a C# member the sim omits is DEAD IN THE GAME SOURCE ITSELF -- zero overrides, zero producers, zero callers anywhere under src/ -- the correct verdict is `faithful`, not `waiver`. PROMPT.md v6 item 3, which the relic stream itself wrote, settles the principle for the mirror-image case: 'a waiver is in-scope-adjacent and declined, and here there is no source behaviour to be faithful to.' A waiver claims something in scope was deliberately not audited; here there is nothing to decline, because the member provably cannot fire in any run of the shipping game and cannot become live by porting more content -- it would take a change to the game's own source. `faithful` also states the stronger and more useful fact: the two codebases have the SAME observable. Before this pass the relic tier split 8 waivers against 5 faithfuls on identical reasoning; these entries are now all `faithful` (binding rule 3). NOTE: this ruling does NOT touch MULTIPLAYER gates (`player != base.Owner`, `Players.Count == 1`), which stay `waiver` -- the shared contract names multiplayer as out of scope outright, and unlike a dead member a player count really can differ in the shipping game; the sim simply does not model that mode. AT THIS SITE: The finding is unchanged and still executed: `grep -rn 'AfterRemoved' 'src/Core/Models/Relics/'` returns ZERO matches -- not one of the game's relic models overrides it -- and `hasattr(Relic, 'after_removed')` is False on the sim side. So Burning Blood cannot be doing anything on removal in the game either and the sim's omission provably cannot change an outcome. Same basis and same verdict as audit/records/relic/unsettling_lamp.json N1 (power.IsVisible) and audit/records/relic/calling_bell.json G4 (Hook.ShouldAddToDeck), both of which the fix pass moved to `faithful` at the same time. ONLY THE VERDICT CHANGES. Rule 7: sts2_rl/relics/base.py, RelicCmd.cs and the two cited records are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: `StarterRelic ?? base.Owner.Relics.First(r => r.Rarity == Starter).Id` and the two [SavedProperty] members (TouchOfOrobas.cs:53-99, 154-158)
guards.rationale: C# lets the relic be SET UP before it is obtained -- SetupForPlayer(player) (TouchOfOrobas.cs:134-145) latches StarterRelic/UpgradedRelic so the offer screen can name them, and AfterObtained then prefers the latched ids over a fresh lookup. The sim models neither member and re-derives the starter at pickup time (touch_of_orobas.py:23-25). Same observable, because the only thing that could change between setup and pickup is the player's starter relic, and no ported path removes or replaces a starter before this relic resolves -- the Orobas shrine offers and grants inside one room. The offer-time half of SetupForPlayer IS ported, just not onto the relic: events/orobas.py:67-71 gates the option on `starter is not None and starter.id in TouchOfOrobas.REFINEMENTS`, which is SetupForPlayer's `return false if no starter` (see N4 for the difference in that condition). The InvalidOperationException guards ('Recursive Core setup called twice!') are structural. Rule 7: events/orobas.py is not hashed here.

guards.what: N4: `GetUpgradedStarterRelic` falls back to `ModelDb.Relic<Circlet>()` for a starter outside RefinementUpgrades (TouchOfOrobas.cs:120-127); the port returns without doing anything (touch_of_orobas.py:26-29), and the shrine will not even offer it
guards.rationale: OTHER CHARACTERS, named and verified. RefinementUpgrades (TouchOfOrobas.cs:29-51) has five entries: BurningBlood->BlackBlood (Ironclad), RingOfTheSnake->RingOfTheDrake (Silent), DivineRight->DivineDestiny (Regent), BoundPhylactery->PhylacteryUnbound (Necrobinder), CrackedCore->InfusedCore (Defect). The sim's REFINEMENTS keeps exactly the Ironclad row (touch_of_orobas.py:18), and the Ironclad's only starting relic is Burning Blood (granted unconditionally at run.py:659), so the fallback arm is unreachable in this sim's scope -- EXECUTED: `circlet` is not even a registered sim relic, so the arm could not be implemented today without porting it. Note the shape difference for the record: C#'s SetupForPlayer returns true for ANY starter and lets GetUpgradedStarterRelic degrade to Circlet, whereas events/orobas.py:67-71 refuses to offer the relic unless the starter is IN the map. Those differ only for a character whose starter is not in the five-entry map, which is not the Ironclad. Waived under the contract's 'characters other than Ironclad' exclusion with the concrete unported thing named (no `circlet` entry exists in the sim relic registry, relics/base.py _RELIC_CLASSES).

Per PROMPT.md v6 binding item 3, the ABSENCE of undo_after_obtained is faithful at every site: the helper has no C# counterpart, nothing in the game un-picks a relic, so a sim lacking it is not diverging from the source. Recorded here because the operational consequence is unusually bad for THIS relic: the conformance runner grants a node's relic and then swaps it for the one the save says was picked (conformance/runner.py's relic resync), and a speculative Touch of Orobas has already destroyed Burning Blood and replaced it with Black Blood by then -- so the swap leaves the run with the wrong starter and DETECTOR 3's act-boundary HP assertion drifts by the Black Blood/Burning Blood heal difference every combat. That is a tooling defect to log, not a fidelity gap. Rule 7: conformance/runner.py is not hashed here.
